title: Prompt healthcheck orchestrator and configurable grace-period regression latch
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add a prompt healthcheck orchestrator that runs lightweight probe suites per prompt-set, surfaces degradation signals, and triggers a configurable grace-period latch to delay automated rollback and allow staged mitigations. No public API changes.
description: Motivation: Some recent regressions are transient or caused by downstream infra noise; automatic rollbacks are too aggressive for low-severity degradations. This PR introduces a prompt healthcheck orchestrator that continuously evaluates a lightweight probe suite against active prompt-sets and emits a graded degradation signal. A new configurable grace-period regression latch aggregates degradation score and only escalates to an automatic rollback after passing severity and duration thresholds. The orchestrator supports pluggable probes (semantic similarity, token-level drift, response-length anomaly), per-prompt weighting, and a short-circuit path for high-confidence hard failures. Implementation summary: added healthcheck orchestrator service, probe adapters, a lightweight in-memory scoring window, a grace-period latch controller, and CI hooks to run smoke probes on PRs touching prompt definitions. Testing: unit tests for probe adapters and latch logic, integration test that spins up a fake probe runner and simulates transient versus sustained degradation, and a smoke CI job exercising the end-to-end orchestrator on a small sample prompt-set. Rollout plan: feature-gate the orchestrator with an opt-in flag in config; start in dry-run mode for 48h, then enable soft-fail handling before automated rollbacks are permitted. Checklist: - [x] Implement orchestration core and probe adapters - [x] Add per-prompt weighting and grading logic - [x] Add grace-period latch with duration and severity thresholds - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Add CI smoke job - [x] Update docs and runbook - [x] Stage dry-run rollout and enable telemetry Caveats: scoring heuristics are intentionally conservative and will be tuned over the dry-run period. Long-term plan includes adding historical cohort baselines and probe-level calibration.
